title: July Job Market Summary
body:
In July 2026, the total number of employed persons increased by 108,000 YoY. The employment rate for ages 15-64 also rose by 0.1%p to 70.3%.

However, the situation is different for the youth. The youth employment rate (ages 15-29) was 44.2%, down 1.6%p YoY.

While the overall market isn't collapsing, first-time job seekers may find it harder than the average stats suggest.

Sectoral gaps are also wide: growth in services, but continued decline in manufacturing and construction.

### Summary
Overall employment is holding up, but youth and certain industries face ongoing challenges.
source: Ministry of Employment and Labor · 2026.07 Trends

title: Core Employment Indicators
body:
■ Total Employed: 29.14M (+108K)
The actual number of people working. While it increased, the distribution across industries is uneven.

■ 15-64 Employment Rate: 70.3% (+0.1%p)
Based on OECD standards. The overall labor market remains relatively stable.

■ Unemployment Rate: 2.6% (+0.2%p)
Low unemployment doesn't always mean easy hiring, as those who stop searching are excluded from this stat.

■ Labor Force Participation: 65.0% (Unchanged)
Percentage of population aged 15+ who are either working or actively seeking work.

title: Youth Metrics to Watch
body:
■ Youth Employment Rate: 44.2% (-1.6%p)
Overall rate rose, but youth rate fell due to reduced hiring and a strong preference for experienced workers.

■ Youth 'Not in Labor Force': 367K (-69K)
Refers to those resting without specific activity. Decreasing for 6 months, but must be viewed alongside the employment rate drop.

### Seekers' Perspective
Don't blame only yourself for bad results; sometimes the market is just tough. Adapt by widening your target roles and focusing on specific skill requirements.

title: Hiring by Industry
body:
■ Services (+295K)
- Healthcare/Social Work (+173K)
- Public Admin (+46K)
- Finance/Insurance (+34K)
- Prof/Scientific/Tech (-44K)

■ Manufacturing (-68K)
Decline continues but at a slower pace. Growth in Electronics/Comm, decline in Textiles/Autos.

■ Construction (-5.7K)
Weakness persists, though the rate of decline has slowed slightly.

title: Service Planning / PM
subtitle: Architects of Business Value
body:
■ Responsibilities
Connecting user problems with business goals to decide what to build and improve.

■ Key Tasks
- Identifying user pain points and defining requirements
- Designing user flows (Wireframing)
- Coordinating dev/design schedules
- Analyzing data post-launch

■ Key Skills
- Logical thinking and problem definition
- Data literacy (SQL, GA4)
- Communication and collaboration

■ Portfolio Tip
Show the flow: Problem → Evidence → Hypothesis → Planning → Execution → Result → Reflection.

title: Android Development
subtitle: Implementing Mobile Experiences
body:
■ Responsibilities
Developing and operating applications for the Android smartphone environment.

■ Key Skills
- Proficiency in Kotlin
- UI design with Jetpack Compose or XML
- Modern architecture: ViewModel, Coroutine, Flow
- REST API and DB (Room) usage

■ Portfolio Tip
Write a great GitHub README. Emphasize why you chose certain technologies and how you solved specific bugs.

title: D-3 to D-1 Checklist
body:
■ Research
Understand your role in the business rather than just memorizing company history.

■ Re-read Job Posting
Connect one specific experience to each key responsibility and required skill listed.

■ D-1 Checklist
- Review your resume/cover letter
- Practice 1-min intro & motivation
- Prepare 3 reverse questions
- Check equipment for online interviews

title: The STAR Structure
body:
Follow this for behavioral interview questions:

■ S (Situation): What was the context?
■ T (Task): What was your role and the problem?
■ A (Action): What specific actions did YOU take?
■ R (Result): What was the outcome? (Quantified if possible)

Note: Many guides emphasize providing evidence and metrics for your results.

title: First Step to Successful Change
body:
### Positive Reframing of Reasons
Bad: 'My previous company was a mess.'
Good: 'I achieved X in my current role, and I want to contribute to your growth environment.'

■ Record Habits
Don't prep only when quitting. Update your solved problems, metrics, and tools every quarter.

■ Quantify Achievements
Instead of 'Responded to customer queries,' use 'Reduced repetitive queries by 24% through FAQ reorganization.'

title: Common Job Terms
body:
### JD (Job Description)
Content explaining the role and requirements in a job posting.

### Onboarding
The process of helping new hires adapt to the organization.

### KPI (Key Performance Indicator)
Metrics used to evaluate the success of an organization or activity.

### JD vs. Resume
JD is what they want; Resume is what you have. Matching them is the key.
